ancestors.notes: Russian adstrate: long Volga-Ural contact and Soviet-era lexicon.
Tatar adstrate: closely related neighbouring Kipchak literary language.
Arabic adstrate: religious vocabulary via the Islamic literary tradition.

name: Bashkir
notes:
Bashkir in Cyrillic script (Russia). Distinctive interdentals: Ҙ = /ð/, Ҫ = /θ/ — unusual among Turkic and a defining contrast against Tatar. Ҡ = /q/ (uvular stop); Ғ = /ʁ/; Ң = /ŋ/; Һ = /h/. Nine vowels with front/back harmony: а /a/, ә /æ/, о /o/, ө /ø/, у /u/, ү /y/, ы /ɯ/, и /i/, е /e/.

⟨е⟩ is iotated /je/ word-initially, after another vowel, and after a soft or hard sign (Wikipedia, "Bashkir language", alphabet table); it is the plain vowel /e/ after a consonant. Word-initial iotation is keyed on position (⟨е⟩ → /je/ word-initially, /e/ by default). After-vowel iotation is written as the harmonic digraphs ае, ое, ые, ие, ее, әе and өе, because the shared orthographic-vowel table does not classify the Turkic Cyrillic letters ә and ө, so an after-vowel position could not see them; ⟨ье⟩ and ⟨ъе⟩ are keyed directly as digraphs for the same reason.

⟨у⟩ and ⟨ү⟩ spell the glide /w/ when they follow a back and a front vowel respectively; as vowels they occur only in the first syllable (Wikipedia, "Bashkir language", alphabet table). The harmonic sequences are written as digraphs — ау оу ыу уу and әү өү үү еү иү — for the same reason: the shared orthographic-vowel table does not classify ә ө ү at all.

⟨ъ⟩ and ⟨ь⟩ represent a glottal stop or syllable break rather than a full consonant (Wikipedia, "Bashkir language"); this spec maps them to the empty string on their own, since the engine has no glottal-stop segment to assign them, while still keying the ⟨ъе⟩/⟨ье⟩ sequences to /je/ so the following vowel is not silently dropped. ⟨ё⟩ /jo/, ⟨ц⟩ /ts/, ⟨щ⟩ /ʃtʃ/ and ⟨в⟩ /v/ carry Russian loanwords.

Known residual: ⟨и⟩ is /i/ in the first syllable and an underlying /ij/ elsewhere, especially in open syllables (Wikipedia, "Bashkir language"). The second reading is not declared because the positional vocabulary has no first-syllable position, and approximating it with word-initial would mis-fire on every polysyllable.

stress.notes: Bashkir default stress is word-final (-1). Certain grammatical endings (negation, question) are unstressed; not modeled here. Source: Poppe (1964), Johanson & Csató (1998).
